name: Nearest Beautiful Number (easy version)
description: It is a simplified version of problem F2. The difference between them is the constraints (F1: $$$k \le 2$$$, F2: $$$k \le 10$$$). You are given an integer $$$n$$$. Find the minimum integer $$$x$$$ such that $$$x \ge n$$$ and the number $$$x$$$ is $$$k$$$- beautiful . A number is called $$$k$$$- beautiful if its decimal representation having no leading zeroes contains no more than $$$k$$$ different digits. E.g. if $$$k = 2$$$, the numbers $$$3434443$$$, $$$55550$$$, $$$777$$$ and $$$21$$$ are $$$k$$$- beautiful whereas the numbers $$$120$$$, $$$445435$$$ and $$$998244353$$$ are not.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Then $$$t$$$ test cases follow. Each test case consists of one line containing two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^9$$$, $$$1 \le k \le 2$$$).
output_specification: For each test case output on a separate line $$$x$$$ — the minimum $$$k$$$- beautiful integer such that $$$x \ge n$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1560F1 — Nearest Beautiful Number (easy version) [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
